authorization: Joseph, 2026-09-18: implementation and bounded tail validation
non_relaxation: These thresholds are frozen before execution. Any change alters this file's sha256, which every receipt records, so a threshold relaxed after seeing a failure is visible in the evidence rather than silent.

release_tiers.tier_1_cross_device: widths where the full cross-device gate passes are released under the UNCHANGED criteria; nothing is dropped for them
release_tiers.tier_2_gpu_only: widths where a cross-device sub-check fails are released only if (a) every failing sub-check is in exempt_cross_device_subchecks, (b) the whole GPU-only battery passes, and (c) the receipt flags them tier 2 so any later result can be read with that scope
release_tiers.never_exempt: Any cross-device sub-check outside that list failing is a hard stop, including the device-independent identity of initial weights. A sub-check that PASSES at a tier-2 width is required to keep passing; a regression there is a hard stop.

V4_float64_adam_reference.weights: all 42, extended from the key bias alone

V5a_finite_difference_plateau.rationale: A per-width plateau check, so the tolerance is justified AT each width instead of extrapolated from the widths measured on 2026-09-18. No plateau means the finite-difference estimate is uninformative there, and the width is not released rather than being waved through.

measured_basis.margin: 5e-3 is about eight times the worst measured maximum, leaving room for degradation at widths beyond those measured while staying four times tighter than the 2e-2 asserted in the first draft, which no realistic error could have tripped

V6_cross_device_recorded.note: the dropped requirements become measured quantities reported per width

V7_permutation_invariance.rationale: not bitwise: floating-point addition is not associative, so a permuted segment sum legitimately differs in the last places

V9_overlap_calibration.note: where the cross-device gate passes, the GPU-only battery must also pass

stage_a_validation.what: two arms with identical specs but different labels must produce bitwise-identical weights and training loss after N steps
stage_a_validation.why_bitwise: identical configurations under determinism have no licence to differ at all; anything else is arm-label-dependent state leaking into the run

stage_b_pilot.what: one duplicate arm carried through the pilot, contributing a contrast that must be zero; its measured value bounds spurious contrast in the ENDPOINT's units

V13_duplicate_arm_null.rationale: No rigorous propagation from weight-space residuals to the closure statistic is available, so the end-to-end bound is measured instead. Split into two stages because the validation run has no closure statistic to measure and the pilot does.
V13_duplicate_arm_null.amended: 2026-09-18, BEFORE any validation execution and with no results seen: the original single-stage wording asked for a closure number that the validation stage does not produce. Recorded here rather than silently reinterpreted at run time.

withdrawn_claims.errors_cancel_in_paired_contrasts: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-18. The earlier plan said an error surviving every check would be arm-symmetric and therefore cancel in a paired contrast. That is not established: an undetected error can be arm-correlated below the resolution of V8, and no propagation from weight-space residuals to the closure statistic is offered. What is claimed instead is bounded and measured: residuals are bounded at the stated tolerances, their measurable arm-asymmetry is bounded by V8, and V13 bounds spurious contrast end to end in the endpoint's own units. Residual risk below those bounds is acknowledged, not argued away.

allocation.counting: ElapsedRaw x gpus over every submission that reaches RUNNING, receipt or not. Repaired submissions count as retries and consume these limits.
stop_conditions: submission cap or GPU-hour ceiling reached, even mid-ladder
a tier-2 width whose failing cross-device sub-checks are not a subset of the exempt list
